listening_material_parts.scenario: A woman moving to London phones a relocation service to register her details and property requirements.

turns.speaker: speaker1
turns.text: This is the IELTS listening test. You will hear four different recordings and you will have to answer questions on what you hear. There will be time for you to read the instructions and the questions, and you will have a chance to check your work. You will hear each recording once only. The test is in four parts. At the end of the test you will be given two minutes to check all of your answers. Part one. You will hear a telephone conversation between a woman who is moving to London and an employee of a relocation service. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5. Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 5.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: London Relocation Services, Daniel speaking. How may I help you?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Good morning. My family and I are moving to London later this year and I wonder if you can help.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Sure. First of all, I'll need to get some personal details. May I take your full name, please?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: It's Anna Woods.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Thanks. Where are you moving from?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Northern Ireland, just outside Belfast.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Right. And what's your current address?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: It's 118 Fordyce. I'll spell that for you. It's F-O-R-D-Y-C-E and that's in Ballysillan.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: And what's the postcode?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: It's BT14 9BJ.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: All right. And could I take a contact phone number?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: I'll give you my mobile number as you can get me on that anytime. It's 07840051963.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Great, got that. Now, we always like to get a bit more information about the families that we're moving. It helps with the search. Are you moving for work?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Yes. My husband's just got a new job in London.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: And what about you? Do you work?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Well, I've been working as a teaching assistant recently, but I'm actually a qualified nurse and I'd like to get back into that if possible.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Right. And do you have any children?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Yes, a son. So we need to find a school for him.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Is it a secondary school you'll be looking for?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: I said secondary, but let me correct that. He is still in primary school.

turns.speaker: speaker1
turns.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10. Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Fine. So let's go on to talk about your requirements for the property. Do you have a preferred location? Is your husband's job in the centre?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: No, it's in east London, but we'd rather live somewhere quieter.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Sure, there are some lovely areas in the South.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: OK, that sounds great. Now my husband doesn't want to spend too long commuting to work every day.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: So I imagine that ideally he'd like to be not too far from a station then.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Yes, he drives now, but I guess that's not going to be possible and he's not keen on buses.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Oh, what about you or your son? Do you have any preferences? Does your son do any sport for example?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: He's quite active, so I'm sure he'd love a park nearby to run around in. He doesn't do swimming or anything like that.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Great.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: So what sort of property do you have in mind, a flat or a house?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: We have friends in an amazing flat, but as we've always lived in a house, we'll stick with the latter.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: OK. And sizewise, how many bedrooms would you like?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Well, there's just myself, my husband and our son.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: So you definitely need a two-bedroom property.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: That's right, two bedrooms at least.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: But how about having a guest room? I might be able to find a three-bedroom property for you.

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Yes, that would be ideal. We're sure to have family visiting often.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Alright, I've made a note of that. Now, are there any other requirements for your new property?

turns.speaker: speaker3
turns.text: Well, it's not essential, but it'd be handy to have an office for when my husband works from home. It doesn't need to be a big one. I guess it all comes down to budget.

turns.speaker: speaker2
turns.text: Yes. Okay, Anna, well I've certainly got enough to be getting on with and I will...

turns.speaker: speaker1
turns.text: That is the end of part one. You now have half a minute to check your answers to part one. Now turn to part two.
